response.markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Training margins do not establish macro validation HR@10 gains. Ranking validation remains necessary. (2) Feedback favors recent, repeated, specific evidence. It does not establish ownership, compatibility or purchase intent. (3) Compatibility hooks permit controlled architecture comparisons. Missing observations must remain unavailable rather than healthy-looking zeros.

**Related work.** (1) The supplied [Spotify study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) distinguishes low-rank last-item FMC from count-based history-aware PCTM. Neither establishes benefits for the proposed hybrid. (2) [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.09152) establishes additive multi-lag factorization precedent. Originality therefore lies mainly in the controlled SASRec integration. (3) [Liu et al.](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042) identify availability confounding in shuffling, while [sampling analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263) cautions against equating sampled and catalog rankings. Diagnostics need controls and cannot replace pinned selection.

These insights suggest three directions: explicit recency modeling, controlled behavioral diagnostics, and evidence-grounded interpretation.

### Framework

| Component | Existing evidence | Gap and proposed response |
|---|---|---|
| Sequence representation | SASRec, FMC and FOSSIL | Test an additive history branch |
| Reliance on history | Training margins | Compare recent and matched older deletions |
| Recommendation meaning | Qualitative feedback | Separate supported evidence from unknown prerequisites |
| Selection | Fixed sampled HR@10 | Preserve protocol and report category effects |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Recency-weighted pairwise residual | 2/6/5 | Originality: controlled integration, strong precedent. Potential: inexpensive complementary evidence, redundancy or popularity shortcuts. Difficulty: small branch, causal scoring and checkpoint synchronization require care. |
| Last-item-preserving history dropout | 3/6/2 | Originality: targeted augmentation, familiar method. Potential: robustness, possible evidence loss. Difficulty: simple masking, careful compaction. |
| Popularity-matched rank diagnostics | 4/6/3 | Originality: focused controls, established statistics. Potential: interpretable failures, uncertain optimization benefit. Difficulty: modest sampling code, costly catalog scoring. |

### Selected idea: recency-weighted pairwise residual

At 0% progress, retain this reversible extension, with reduced novelty claims. Add rank-32 directed transitions pooled with normalized exponential weights, initially tau=5. Repetition increases contribution; interpreting this as current intent remains unsupported.

```text
initialize random source factors, zero target factors, gate alpha=1
for each category and causal training prefix:
    context = SASRec(prefix)
    history = masked normalized exponential source recurrence
    score = contextual_score + alpha * history · target(item)
    optimize baseline loss on valid next-item positions
save configuration, checkpoint and matching generated predictor
```

Zero target factors preserve baseline initial scores while receiving task gradients; avoid multiplying tiny gates and tiny factors. Track branch/base score RMS, factor norms, updates and gate trajectories; inspect actual regularization rather than assuming Adam cancels scaling.

Preserve splits, seeds, routing and epoch defaults. Retain diagnostic interfaces, restore model mode, and report sample counts and unavailable values. Update predictor generation and verify causal pooling, padding, final-position scores and strict reload equivalence. Prioritize baseline versus residual; then compare last-item/uniform pooling and residual ablation within a declared budget. A parameter-matched SASRec control addresses capacity. Select solely by pinned macro HR@10; popularity-stratified diagnostics and twenty-user feedback remain explanatory, and repeated validation risks selection overfitting.

idea.description: Add a rank-32, recency-weighted directed item-transition residual to each category's SASRec model. Jointly train combined scores, preserve the original routing and evaluation protocol, and treat this as a controlled extension of established factorization methods rather than a novel model family.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests that broad historical similarity sometimes outweighs recent specific evidence. An explicit history branch makes that hypothesis testable, but improved recency sensitivity need not improve ranking or establish immediate purchase intent. FMC, PCTM and FOSSIL provide distinct precedents; none establishes gains for this SASRec combination on the four requested datasets.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve preprocessing seed=0, training seed=42, all four datasets, original splits and dataset routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all checkpoints, configurations and generated working/predict.py remain beneath the trial directory. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS, whose supplied environment default is 200, and retain single-GPU execution. No hidden test access, extra datasets or pretrained weights.

Use separate rank-32 source and target embeddings with padding_idx=0. Initialize source coordinates independently with standard deviation 1/sqrt(32), target embeddings to zero, and the per-category learned scalar gate so softplus(gate)=1. This makes the initial residual zero while permitting initial task gradients into target rows; source and gate task gradients initially vanish and can develop after targets update. Both factors must not start at zero. This is a reproducible initialization choice, not an established optimum. Log branch/base score RMS and update magnitudes before changing initialization.

Set tau=5 and decay=exp(-1/tau), measured in retained interaction positions rather than elapsed time. For each supplied truncated sequence, initialize float32 numerator n and mass z to zero. At position t, m=(sequence[:,t]!=0); update n=where(m, decay*n+source(sequence[:,t]), n), z=where(m, decay*z+1, z), and h=n/z.clamp_min(1e-8). Broadcast masks over features. Stack outputs without detaching. Padding contributes no mass or decay; the current observed item contributes when predicting its next item. Reset state for every supplied sequence. Repeated items contribute repeatedly, which may amplify preference evidence or popularity and repeated-consumption shortcuts.

Keep the baseline loss, optimizer, sampling, history length and contextual regularization initially. Define the baseline regularizer explicitly over its original parameters so adding tables does not silently introduce a full-table penalty. Apply no explicit L2 or weight decay to the new factors and gate in the initial trial; retain applicable original optimizer settings on baseline parameters. Inspect whether baseline regularization is squared, unsquared, coupled or decoupled, and record it. If later adding branch regularization, declare its expression, reduction and coefficient, and avoid accidentally applying both a loss penalty and optimizer shrinkage. Adam normalization can mitigate gradient scaling but does not guarantee useful updates under epsilon, noise or shrinkage.

Have log2feats return concatenated contextual features of dimension D and history features of dimension 32, giving B x L x (D+32). predict_score splits at D and computes the contextual dot product plus softplus(gate) times the history/target dot product. Support paired items B x L x 2 and final features B x (D+32) with candidates B x K through the same scoring function. Preserve view.model as the actual trained module and view.item_emb as the contextual item table; document that its alignment diagnostic excludes the transition tables. Adapt diagnostic feature-dimension assumptions.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions grounded in measured quantities, with valid-position counts and null values for unavailable observations. Restore the model's previous training mode after diagnostics. Use only permitted histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions; ignore the generic input examples containing unavailable ratings, reviews, prices, stores or item categories. Raw margins remain score-scale dependent. Popularity strata must derive exclusively from training interactions.

In eval mode without gradients, verify recurrence against a direct weighted sum; test left padding, empty and singleton histories, and truncation. Compare scores[:, -1, :] against final-feature scoring on identical candidates, and repeat after strict checkpoint reload using the serialized architecture, dimensions, decay and gate. For prefix comparisons, hold retained histories and positional indices identical. Empty histories must produce finite outputs; their contextual behavior must be explicitly defined if the baseline attention implementation cannot handle all-padding sequences. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the full architecture and load all parameters and persistent buffers.

Prioritize a matched baseline-versus-residual comparison. Predeclare the maximum number of fits and validation queries in the trial configuration before execution; no numeric trial cap was supplied in the report. If budget remains, compare last-item, uniform and exponential pooling with identical factors, loss and optimization, followed by a parameter-matched wider SASRec. Transition-only, tied-table and frozen-branch blend controls are useful later, not mandatory initial searches. Evaluate lambda=0 ablation and combined scoring on identical validation users and candidates; do not interpret inference ablation as equivalent to separately training SASRec. Record per-category and macro HR@10, training cost, gate/norm trajectories, residual/base RMS and rank changes. Account for all training and diagnostic GPU time within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Keep the host evaluator unchanged. Limit adaptive validation reuse; paired within-category user bootstrap intervals, if available, are descriptive after selection and conditional on fixed candidates and seed. Twenty simulator users support qualitative inspection only.
idea.pseudocode:
For each routed category:
  construct baseline SASRec with its original settings
  construct source[items,32] ~ Normal(0,1/sqrt(32)); target[items,32] = 0
  zero padding rows; set gate = inverse_softplus(1); decay = exp(-1/5)
  retain baseline optimizer settings; explicitly exclude new factors/gate from decay
  for each baseline batch (None, sequence, positive, negative):
    context = causal_SASRec(sequence)
    n = zeros(B,32,float32); z = zeros(B,1,float32)
    history = []
    for t in sequence positions:
      m = (sequence[:,t] != 0)[:,None]
      n = where(m, decay*n + source(sequence[:,t]).float(), n)
      z = where(m, decay*z + 1, z)
      history.append(n / clamp_min(z,1e-8))
    features = concatenate(context, stack(history), last_dimension)
    scores = shared_predict_score(features, stack(positive,negative))
    optimize original loss at valid next-item positions plus original baseline regularizer
  save full state and architecture configuration; generate matching predictor
  verify direct recurrence, final-position scoring and strict reload equivalence
Compare baseline and combined model under pinned validation; select by equal-weight macro HR@10.
If the declared budget permits, run pooling and capacity controls with identical evaluation candidates.
Interpret branch ablation, perturbations and qualitative feedback as diagnostics, not user-intent measurements.

originality.positive: The explicit SASRec integration and matched diagnostic controls form a useful, testable combination for this task.
originality.negative: Directed low-rank transitions, additive preference components, multi-lag pooling and recency weighting have substantial precedent, including FMC and FOSSIL.

future_potential.positive: A small explicit branch supports controlled investigation of when recent transition evidence complements contextual sequence models.
future_potential.negative: It may duplicate SASRec, exploit popularity or repeated-item shortcuts, and improve sampled ranking without improving catalog-wide usefulness or immediate acceptance.

code_difficulty.positive: The core branch needs two embedding tables, a stable recurrence and an additive scorer, with no additional data acquisition.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable causal training, initialization and regularization, feature-shape compatibility, diagnostic adaptation, generated inference and checkpoint equivalence require substantial care.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: The supplied article and implementation summaries distinguish low-rank last-item FMC/FMC+ from history-aware count-based PCTM.
Motivates testing simple transition evidence and controlled recency baselines.
limitations: Its reported datasets and full-catalog ranking conditions differ from this four-category sampled HR@10 task.
Does not establish a recency-weighted low-rank history hybrid or an additive SASRec residual.

related_work.title: FOSSIL: Factored Similarity Models with Markov Chains for Sparse Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines long-term item-history preference with additive factorized contributions from recent interactions.
Provides direct precedent for multi-lag low-rank scoring and discusses the related FPMC formulation.
limitations: Its learned global and personalized lag weights differ from the proposed fixed exponential pooling.
Does not establish complementarity with SASRec or gains under the pinned RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: Liu et al., RecSys 2025: availability-aware history shuffling
contributions: The supplied summary identifies item availability as a confound in arbitrary sequence shuffling.
limitations: Edited-history sensitivity does not identify causal changes in user preferences.
Availability constraints do not remove every distribution shift caused by perturbation.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems
contributions: Analyzes limitations of sampled recommendation evaluation and motivates distinguishing sampled rankings from full-catalog behavior.
limitations: Does not justify replacing the task's pinned sampled HR@10 selection criterion.
Does not establish which proposed architecture will perform best on these four categories.

related_work.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
contributions: Distinguishes decoupled weight decay from loss-based L2 regularization under adaptive optimization.
Supports explicitly auditing how regularization applies to new transition factors.
limitations: Does not prescribe an optimal penalty, initialization or optimizer for this branch.
Small analytical gradients alone do not determine actual adaptive optimizer updates.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Provides precedent for residual paths whose initially zero gates learn from nonzero branch outputs.
Helps distinguish zero-gate initialization from the proposed nonzero-gate, zero-target-factor initialization.
limitations: A zero gate with zero branch output would not receive the same initial task-learning signal.
Its results do not establish an optimal residual initialization for sequential recommendation.

related_work.title: PyTorch Module documentation
contributions: Documents evaluation mode and state_dict handling of parameters and persistent buffers.
Supports reproducible scorer equivalence and strict checkpoint reload checks.
limitations: Correct serialization does not guarantee that generated inference reconstructs the same architecture or preprocessing.
Evaluation mode alone does not disable gradient recording.
